record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.original_question: For finite zero sequences A and B in L2_a(D), let Phi_A and Phi_B be the Green-potential functions associated with the zero divisors G_A and G_B. If A is contained in B, is Phi_A(z) ≤ Phi_B(z) for every z in D?

evidence.quote: We write here Phi_A instead of Phi_GA, for a given zero sequence A.
Conjecture 2.2. If A, B are two finite zero sequences for L2_a(D) having A ⊂ B, then Phi_A ≤ Phi_B holds on D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb{C}$ and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space of holomorphic functions $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ with $\|f\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty$, where $dA$ is normalized area measure. A finite sequence $A = (a_1,\dots,a_n)$ of points in $\mathbb{D}$ (with multiplicities) is called a zero sequence for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$. To such a finite zero sequence one associates the canonical (contractive) zero divisor $G_A \in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$: the unique extremal function solving $\sup\{\operatorname{Re} f(0) : f \in L^2_a(\mathbb{D}),\ \|f\|=1,\ f \text{ vanishes on } A \text{ with the prescribed multiplicities}\}$ (equivalently, $G_A$ is the reproducing-kernel-based contractive divisor of the zero-based invariant subspace generated by $A$). Define the Green-potential function $\Phi_A : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{R}$ associated with $G_A$ by
$$\Phi_A(z) \;=\; \int_{\mathbb{D}} \log|G_A(w)|^2 \, G(z,w)\, dA(w),$$
where $G(z,w)$ is the Green function of $\mathbb{D}$ for the Laplacian (so that $\Delta_z \Phi_A(z) = \log|G_A(z)|^2$ in the distributional sense, with zero boundary values).

Question: If $A$ and $B$ are two finite zero sequences for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ with $A \subset B$ (as multisets), does the inequality
$$\Phi_A(z) \;\le\; \Phi_B(z)$$
hold for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any publication that resolves the monotonicity conjecture $\Phi_A \le \Phi_B$ for $A \subset B$ in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$. The conjecture appears in Hedenmalm's open-problems survey and is referenced in subsequent surveys on the Bergman space, but no proof or counterexample was located. Status is reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems in Bergman space theory by Aleman, Hedenmalm and Richter.
status_evidence.claim: The monotonicity question for zero-divisor Green potentials is discussed among open problems in Bergman space theory; no resolution is indicated.

status_evidence.title: Beurling's Theorem for the Bergman space
status_evidence.snippet: Uses positivity of the biharmonic Green function to establish contractive divisor properties.
status_evidence.claim: Related positivity/biharmonic tools are used for contractive divisors, but the specific monotonicity-of-potentials conjecture is not asserted as proved.
